derivation: Generated by `python tools/board_manifest.py` (this board's row, read through tools/import_board.py) from the vendor's own EAGLE 9.6.2 board file, elements J2 (1X06_NO_SILK), J3 (1X06_NO_SILK). Pad centres are the coordinates the file states, in millimetres, with EAGLE's upward Y axis flipped once against a 25.40 x 25.40 mm outline taken from layer 20 (Dimension), plus a 1.0 mm margin. Pad names are the net each pad is on, from <signals>. Nothing here was measured off an image. Scaled at 8.0 px/mm.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the sources named in `pindefs`, and each pad's `chip_pin_from` says which; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. webui/boards/esp32c6.py describes the ESP32-C6, and its table is keyed by the labels of XIAO-ESP32-C6-DIP, XIAO-ESP32-C6-SMD, which are not this board's; no level is read through it for any pad here. The pin view reads a pad's level at its own `chip_index` instead, so a pad with one answers for itself and a pad without one is reported as not modelled.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the sources in `packages`, at those revisions; a board file's `sha256:` is the first twelve hex of the sha256 of its text, newlines as LF. The board-support package names a pin by a pad's label. The vendor's board file names one by copper: the chip pad the pad's net reaches, directly or through one resistor in series, read against the datasheet table its `pin_table` cites. A net on pads that table gives no GPIO says so in `why_null`; one on a pad it does not transcribe, or named for a GPIO it does not reach, is refused. Each resolved pad's `chip_pin_from` names the sources that named it; where two disagree the pad is null and `disputed_by` names them. `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the path each trace took.

pin_table.cite: ESP32-C6-MINI-1 & MINI-1U Datasheet v1.5, pp. 10-11, 3.2 Pin Description and Table 3-1 Pin Definitions: No. against the GPIO its Function names

pads.label: V_BATT
pads.why_null: the battery, not a pin of the ESP32-C6: SparkFun's Qwiic_Pocket_Dev_ESP32_C6.sch puts V_BATT on R13 (1M), whose other net, IO1/V_BATT_2, holds U1's `XTAL_32K_N/IO1` (pad 13) and R14 (1M) to GND -- a divider onto IO1 that senses the battery, which the trace does not cross because that net holds more than R13 and the chip

pads.label: GND
pads.why_null: no GPIO: the vendor's board file traces GND -> U1 30 pads = GND (ESP32-C6-MINI-1 & MINI-1U Datasheet v1.5, pp. 10-11, 3.2 Pin Description and Table 3-1 Pin Definitions: No. against the GPIO its Function names)

pads.label: V_USB
pads.why_null: no board-support package covering this board defines this label, and in the vendor's board file this pad's net reaches no pad of the chip, directly or through one resistor in series, whose other net holds only that resistor and the chip's pad

pads.label: 3.3V
pads.why_null: no GPIO: the vendor's board file traces 3.3V -> U1 pad 3 = 3V3 (ESP32-C6-MINI-1 & MINI-1U Datasheet v1.5, pp. 10-11, 3.2 Pin Description and Table 3-1 Pin Definitions: No. against the GPIO its Function names)
